item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00263","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C14","C21","C15"],"selected_candidate_label":"C14","confidence":0.99,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C14 is a concrete and material drafting template. Like the child, it implements a new GATT protocol through an extensive recital sequence covering the original General Agreement, statutory findings, Tariff Commission review, public notice and interagency advice, execution and authentication of the new protocol, activation of Schedule XX, and coordination with the exclusive Cuban agreement. Its operative provisions also supply the child's distinctive Part I structure: incorporation of protocol and schedule concessions, a subdivision making application subject to GATT terms and qualifications, and the same two-part exception for more favorable customs treatment. The child adapts that machinery from Japan's accession protocol to the Sixth Protocol of Supplementary Concessions. C21 and C15 are strong earlier versions of the same architecture, but C14 is temporally closer and matches the child's wording and operative organization more
